name: copy-field
title: Copy field
purpose: A read-only value the reader takes somewhere else, with a button that copies it.
whenToUse: For a value the reader will paste into a terminal or another tool: a branch name, a commit hash, a path, a command.
When the value is one line. A long one is cut short with an ellipsis and still copies whole.
whenNotToUse: For a value the reader can change. Use a text input in a field.
For several lines, such as a log or a diff. Show them in a pre element.
For a value nobody needs to copy. Write it as plain text.
For a secret that must stay hidden. This component always shows its value.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and as wide as its container, with the button at its natural width. Limit the width on the container.

accessibility: The value is an input element with type="text" and the readonly attribute, never disabled. It stays in the tab order, its text can be selected, and the arrow keys scroll a long value.
Name the input with a label element, usually by putting the copy field inside ds-field after its ds-field__label, or with aria-label when the view has no room for a visible label.
The button is a ds-button with the visible label Copy. Give it an aria-label that names the value, such as Copy branch name, so several on one view can be told apart.
Keep an empty ds-copy-field__status element with role="status" in the page from the start. role="status" is a polite live region, the same as aria-live="polite".
After a copy, the app sets the status text to say what was copied, such as Branch name copied. A screen reader announces it and sighted readers see the same words. Clear the text after a few seconds.
If the copy fails, the app sets the status text to say so and what to do: select the value and copy it by hand.
The confirmation is that text. Do not signal a copy with a colour change alone, and do not move focus away from the button.
